name: Rune-Inscribed Parchment
summary: In the Valley of Trials, Gornek hands aspiring orc shamans a message from Shikrik. It calls them to become spiritual leaders and conduits for elemental spirits.

sections.title: A Summons to the Spirits
sections.body: New orc shamans begin training under veteran overseers in the Valley of Trials. While an initiate performs initial trials for Gornek, he hands them a rune-covered document sent by Shikrik, the local shamanic instructor. The message summons them to deeper communion with the elements. Among the orcs, shamans mediate between the living and their ancestors. The writ marks a move from brute strength toward disciplined reverence for ancestors.

faq.answer: Gornek hands the handwritten message to novice orc shamans in the Valley of Trials. It directs them to report to Shikrik for formal instruction.
Shikrik, the shaman trainer in the Valley of Trials, wrote the parchment to instruct young initiates in the ways of the elements and ancestral spirits.

faq.q: Why are shamans considered chosen among the orcs?
faq.answer: Orc shamans guide their people as spiritual leaders, listening to elemental spirits and acting as conduits for their ancestors. Shikrik reminds apprentices that their duty includes mending allies and wielding the elements' fury against their foes.

angles.text: As a shaman, this note marks your very first step on the path of the elements. Under Shikrik's tutelage, you learn ancestor worship and elemental mastery.
As an orc, you carry on ancestral wisdom in Durotar. The rediscovery of shamanic tradition is central to the new Horde.
